name: grilling-the-plan
description: A method for turning a vague ask into an executable plan that survives contact with reality, by attacking every claim in it — including your own — before anyone builds.

boundary.output: One plan directory: a PLAN.md and a tasks/<ID>/TASK.md per task. Markdown. Nothing else.
boundary.notOutput: No library, no service, no schema, no class, no module, no build step, and no file inside the project you are planning changes to.
boundary.youAreDoingItWrongIf: You are creating a type, module, interface or directory named after anything in this file; or the planned project has acquired a dependency on Grillin; or its build, CI or commit path would break with Grillin uninstalled.
boundary.theGate: scripts/validate-plan.py runs ON the plan directory, from outside it, and belongs on your PATH. It is never vendored into, imported by, or wired into the project being planned.
boundary.whyThisIsFirst: Read cold, the fields below are shaped like a specification to implement: phases[] with ids and outputs, a taskContract with a required[] array and a layout, a reporterContract that reads as an interface, gateChecks[] that reads as a test list. Every one of those is a noun an engineer builds. This block is the boundary, and it is first so it cannot be missed.

coreRule: Adversarial effort spent before building is worth many times the same effort spent after. Three phases produce no plan text at all. They are the highest-value phases.

precedenceLadder.note: your rules file — how work is run
live code, config, data — beats every document
written against a snapshot; assume drift

phases.name: Acknowledge, flag, stop
phases.summary: Restate the ask in your own words. Name what is missing. Flag what would change the plan's shape. Then stop.
phases.output: A paragraph and two or three flags.

phases.name: Inventory — count before you plan
phases.summary: Read-only workers enumerate what exists, partitioned by file ownership so none overlap. Cite file:line. Give counts. Freeze the result.

phases.name: Triage what recon dug up
phases.summary: Sort discovered defects into fix-during-work / needs-a-human-decision / out-of-scope. Never absorb a discovery silently.

phases.name: Grill the documents against the running system
phases.summary: Check every load-bearing claim against the top of the precedence ladder. Hunt for things asserted to exist that do not, staleness, cross-document contradiction, and unflagged assertions.
phases.output: A contradictions register. Expect it to resize the work.

phases.name: Shape first — diagram before prose
phases.summary: A one-screen typed dependency graph, approved before any task text. A wrong diagram costs a minute; the prose it authorises costs hours.

phases.name: Decompose into owned tasks
phases.summary: One folder per task, each a contract: persona, owned files, evidence already gathered, steps, a loop with a cap, evidence-based done, do-NOT list, output contract. Own by file, not by task.

phases.name: Extract recurring context into skills
phases.summary: When the same warning appears in five task files it belongs in a skill. Group by category of work. Carry scar tissue, not generic advice. Load before the first tool call.

phases.name: Design isolation, then find the collision
phases.summary: Separate workspaces are the easy half. List files many tasks want, give each one owner, have everyone else emit a fragment, add an integrator.
phases.output: Isolation model, contended-file table, integrator role.

phases.name: Choose the substrate by measurement
phases.summary: Time a real fan-out on each candidate. Record effective parallelism, not the advertised cap. Find what actually binds. Name what a limit governs before it shapes the plan.

phases.name: Verify the environment the plan assumes
phases.summary: Check that the world the plan describes exists: paths, repos, scripts, permissions, topology, credentials. A failed read is not proof of absence.
phases.output: Corrections to the plan, applied at source.

phases.name: Ship the door with the building
phases.summary: One entry point with a read order, a paste-ready kickoff prompt, persistent memory updated, a published status surface, and hand-off items you cannot do yourself, and a warm restart: a worker halfway through can establish where it got to, not only what the plan is.

scaling.verification: one adversarial pass on the risky task
scaling.phase5Form: reduced — folder, owner, status, done-command; no persona, skills or fragments

scaling.verification: adversarial pass after every build task

scaling.isolation: worktrees + waves + integrator per merge group
scaling.verification: two independent adversarial passes; second must not see the first
two passes per task, plus a completeness critic per track

neverScaleDown.why: grilling documents against the running system is the cheapest phase and catches the most expensive errors
the plan is itself a document, and documents drift — including the one you just wrote

principles.text: Declare precedence before you start. Say out loud when sources disagree.
Count before you plan. Numbers size work; impressions don't.
Shape before prose. Reject a diagram, not a chapter.
Own by file, not by task.
Contended files get one owner; everyone else emits a fragment.

Never certify your own work — and a second pass earns its cost only as a different lens. In the pilot the two passes found disjoint things; on one task pass A returned PASS and pass B found a confirmed high-severity defect, on another pass B added nothing. A second identical sweep does not pay.
Every loop has a cap. Hitting it is a stop-and-report.

Measure constraints; never quote them — then check the instrument, and label the conditions. The pilot's performance tool over-counted, and its headline concurrency figures came from two different workloads on different runs: safe direction, unearned magnitude.
Recurring context becomes a skill, loaded first.
Escalate on decisions, not on findings.

The plan is the artefact of record. Execution amends it — and so do the rules, the skills and the durable memory. Write a deviation the moment it happens; close-out facts legitimately batch at a boundary because they do not exist until the boundary.
Assume amnesia. Anything that lives only in a conversation is already gone. Progress, decisions and corrections must be reconstructable from the repository alone.
Name every agent by role. An unnamed fleet is addressable only by opaque handles, and a role name still means something when the model tier changes.
A reminder that repeats is wallpaper; a reminder that reports is news. Re-pasting rules trains an agent to skip injected text. Compute the reminder from current state and it stays worth reading.

inwardFacing.text: Grill your own artefact last and hardest.
inwardFacing.why: Your plan is a document. Documents drift.

inwardFacing.text: When challenged, verify before you defend.
inwardFacing.why: A challenge can be factually wrong and still be pointing at a real defect. Defending misses it; conceding fixes the wrong thing.

inwardFacing.text: State your own errors plainly and fix them at source.
inwardFacing.why: Capture the pattern, not the event — then search for the same wrong claim everywhere else.

antiPatterns.dont: Start work at the acknowledgement
antiPatterns.because: the restatement is where mismatched understanding surfaces

antiPatterns.dont: Plan from a spec without checking it
antiPatterns.because: specs describe intended systems as though built

antiPatterns.dont: Estimate scope from impression
antiPatterns.because: "several" is not a number

antiPatterns.dont: Write task prose before the shape is approved
antiPatterns.because: you will rewrite all of it

antiPatterns.dont: Let one worker review its own output
antiPatterns.because: it will certify it

antiPatterns.dont: Assign work by task when tasks share files
antiPatterns.because: last writer wins, silently

antiPatterns.dont: Quote a documented limit
antiPatterns.because: it may govern something else

antiPatterns.dont: Treat a failed read as proof of absence
antiPatterns.because: check permissions first

antiPatterns.dont: Log lessons in a growing incident file
antiPatterns.because: fix the document that was wrong

antiPatterns.dont: Turn a review finding into a stop-gate
antiPatterns.because: fixing specified defects is execution

antiPatterns.dont: Ship a plan with no entry point
antiPatterns.because: nobody can start it

antiPatterns.dont: Record a deviation only in the status file
antiPatterns.because: the plan becomes confidently wrong, and a restarted worker trusts it first

antiPatterns.dont: Keep progress in the conversation
antiPatterns.because: a clear or a compaction erases it, and the work gets re-done or skipped

antiPatterns.dont: Run a fleet of identically-named agents
antiPatterns.because: they are addressable only by opaque pane ids, and terminal titles become the only clue to purpose

antiPatterns.dont: Treat an agent's unknown state as done
antiPatterns.because: unknown means unclassified, not finished

antiPatterns.dont: Re-inject the same static reminder every turn
antiPatterns.because: it becomes wallpaper, and teaches that injected text is skippable

antiPatterns.dont: Block a tool call to fix a lost frame
antiPatterns.because: narrowing is not disobedience; denial does not restore the shape

antiPatterns.dont: Treat one independent review as sufficient
antiPatterns.because: a second pass with fresh context overturned all five branches in the pilot

antiPatterns.dont: Let the agent that fixed a defect confirm the fix
antiPatterns.because: that is self-certification, one level down

antiPatterns.dont: Change a gate or its baseline without a receipt
antiPatterns.because: 'the gates pass' silently stops meaning what it did

antiPatterns.dont: Schedule a deletion before its replacements are verified
antiPatterns.because: teardown is where you discover the predecessors nobody finished

antiPatterns.dont: Keep task files loose, or share one folder between tasks
antiPatterns.because: containment, the output contract and the status glob all key on tasks/<ID>/ and break together

antiPatterns.dont: Run a second identical sweep and call it a second pass
antiPatterns.because: it re-finds what the first found; only a different lens or fresh context pays

antiPatterns.dont: Absorb a recurring violation at integration instead of fixing its cause
antiPatterns.because: the pilot's integrator silently cleaned up out-of-folder writes seven times and the cause was never fixed

antiPatterns.dont: Leave an ambient indicator stale
antiPatterns.because: an indicator that never updates is worse than none, because it is believed

outputs.FINDINGS.md: always — what it learned, cited, CONFIRMED vs SUSPECTED, ends with what I did not test
outputs.CHANGES.md: if it changed anything — three lines per file: did / why / risk
outputs.QUESTIONS.md: if blocked or diverged — one question per heading, each with a recommendation

taskContract.statusNote: A line inside TASK.md, updated in place. Not an output file. It is the progress record that survives a lost conversation.
taskContract.loop: do → verify → fix → confirm the fix by someone who did not make it → re-verify, with a stated cap

layout.rule: One folder per task, always, regardless of task count.
layout.theAgentReceivesTheFolder: The directory is the briefing, not a prompt with the task pasted into it. Inbox and outbox are one place.
whyStructural: self-contained — a fact not in the folder or cited from the frozen inventory means the briefing failed
resumable — a worker that lost context re-reads one directory and has the contract, its findings and its status
addressable — status and progress derive from globbing tasks/*/TASK.md; break the layout and the awareness layer goes blind
dependsOnIt: containment scopes writes to the task folder
the output contract files into it
the state reporter globs tasks/*/TASK.md for status
layout.bornMidRun: A task created mid-wave gets its folder before its first artefact. In the pilot all 26 planned folders survived intact; every loose file belonged to a task reality added later.
minimumAtEverySize: a done-command that fails before the work

resumability.premise: Assume every worker forgets. A cleared agent loses its place; a compacted one feels oriented while reasoning from a lossy copy.
resumability.planIsRecord: Deviations amend the plan itself. A dated changelog entry records what changed and why, referenced from the clause it changed.
resumability.receiptNotSubstitute: Recording that something was wrong while the document stays wrong is the failure, not the fix.
resumability.amendedBy: integrator — task agents report divergence in QUESTIONS.md and do not edit the plan
orientationBeforeAction: read the entry point and plan
check git log, git status, worktrees, uncommitted diffs
re-derive completion from checkable evidence, not memory
resumability.editsUsuallyLanded: A worker that appeared to fail has usually already written its edits — verify against the tree before assuming nothing happened.
resumability.test: If every conversation ended now and a new worker cloned the repository, could it tell what was done, what was in flight, and what changed since the plan was written?

default.how: a script spawns workers, collects returns; the orchestrator never sees the middle
costs: blind mid-flight — a worker stuck on an approval prompt looks identical to one thinking, until timeout
no intervention in a running worker
fleet state lives in the orchestrator's context and dies with it

secondary.how: named agents in panes with queryable lifecycle: working | idle | blocked | done | unknown
buys: blocked is observable, so a stall is a fact not a timeout
agents can be read and unblocked mid-flight
the fleet outlives the conversation — one query recovers the roster

monitor.why: herdr agent list is a poll and herdr agent wait is a block; both hold the fleet's state in whichever process asked. herdr has no push events, so durability means writing it down.
publishes: .herdr/state.json — current truth, republished atomically on change
.herdr/transitions.jsonl — append-only, sequence-numbered, one line per CHANGE
rules: it writes and never drives — a monitor that acts is a second orchestrator
transitions only; a ping per poll is a ping nobody reads
since <seq> makes it resumable without replaying the whole history
stale is a state — silence that resembles success is the worst outcome
it does not repeal the rule that idle and unknown are not evidence of completion

measure: effective parallelism on both, not the advertised cap
wall-clock on the same real fan-out, not a synthetic benchmark
recovery cost after a context loss
substrates.invariant: Declare the substrate once and do not mix mid-run. A substrate that uses more than one mechanism internally -- as Smokin does, scripts for control flow and panes for the tasks that need a human -- is ONE substrate, not a mixture, provided the choice between them is declared per task and checkable. Mixing means switching substrate mid-run, not composing one.

third.how: an idempotent tick dispatches from disk and reaps receipts; panes are an escape hatch under a stated rule
buys: survives orchestrator death -- the frontier is re-derived from files, which is what principle 14 has always demanded and never had for a RUNNING fleet
heterogeneous by construction -- a runtime is a row in a JSON file, not a code path
a missing receipt is a message, not an absence, so the result set is total
a generated human surface: STATUS.json is machine truth, PROGRESS.md is rendered only from it
costs: a wrapper on every launch and a capability table to maintain
the tick is only as fresh as its last run -- latency, never lost work
no mid-flight intervention unless a pane was opened for it
third.measured: NOT YET. substrates.measure[] has five rows and not one is filled for Smokin. Under phase 8's own rule it may be declared and used; it may NOT be recommended over the default until those numbers exist for a real fan-out.

invariantAmended.was: Declare the substrate once and do not mix mid-run. Whichever is used, every agent is addressable by a role name — an unnamed fleet is a coincidence, not an organisation.
invariantAmended.now: Declare the substrate once and do not mix mid-run. A substrate that uses more than one mechanism internally -- as Smokin does, scripts for control flow and panes for the tasks that need a human -- is ONE substrate, not a mixture, provided the choice between them is declared per task and checkable. Mixing means switching substrate mid-run, not composing one.
invariantAmended.why: Smokin reads as the forbidden mixture unless it is named as one substrate. Recorded as an amendment rather than an edit: the method's rule is never to resolve a contradiction silently.

awareness.problem: attentional narrowing — a worker deep in one task is doing it correctly and has lost the shape of the plan around it. Not disobedience.
awareness.governingRule: A reminder that repeats is wallpaper; a reminder that reports is news. Compute it from disk — statuses, commits, amendments — so it differs every firing.
awareness.notEnforcement: These reminders never block. Enforcement belongs in _RULES.md; this keeps the agent oriented so the rules have something to be obeyed in service of.

ambient.carries: position only — never rules, which become wallpaper fastest

situational.weight: non-blocking note at the moment of relevance
situational.carries: ownership, contended files, the deployed checkout

punctuated.carries: where, closed, in flight, blocked, what changed, what is next

silent.weight: a written record, never shown to the agent
silent.why: free — no tokens, no interruption — and an agent acknowledged for status updates starts producing them performatively

moments.why: cold or warm start — orient before acting
the literal instant of forgetting; the only moment injected state lands inside the summary rather than being what it drops
one unit closed is the cheapest moment to zoom out
the only work-shaped event available; costs the agent nothing
does the status line reflect what just happened?
never more than one line from knowing where you are
the fact is relevant precisely now

reporterContract: never fail — exit zero on every path
never be slow — no network, no expensive history walks
degrade out loud — silence reads as everything is fine
stay boring — no summarising, no model calls
never touch the plan, the task files or the changelog — its only writes are its own log and the surface it publishes
report claims as claims; mark verified only when the done-command actually ran
awareness.manufacturedEvent: Almost every hook event is harness-shaped, not work-shaped: a turn ending means a turn ended. Principle 13 already obliges the status line to be updated in place, which makes a write to a task file the one observable act coinciding with a real work boundary. Hooking that write yields the event the harness never offered, without adding a second obligation.
awareness.freeMeasurement: Status transitions are timestamped by the filesystem, so NOT STARTED to IN PROGRESS to DONE yields real elapsed time per task and per wave — the phase 8 substrate comparison, collected as a byproduct of working rather than as a benchmark.
awareness.claimsVsEvidence: A DONE status is a claim. It is evidence only once the task's own done-command has run and that fact was recorded. A surface rendering the two alike is a certificate the worker issued to itself, and is worse than no surface because it will be trusted.
awareness.startWith: PreCompact alone — highest value, cannot break anything, and confirming one injection lands beats wiring five that might not.
precompactCarries: where truth lives, so the post-summary worker re-reads rather than recalls
the command that rebuilds the full picture

compactionBoundary.confirmed: Compaction is the instant of forgetting.
compactionBoundary.corrected: An earlier version claimed the pre-compaction hook alone was sufficient. Measured across three compactions: a register re-fired AFTER the boundary held the frame 3/3; verbatim survival of an injection INTO the summary was 1/2.
compactionBoundary.rule: Treat them as one system — inject before so the summary can keep the frame, re-establish after because half the time it did not.
compactionBoundary.note: Session-start registers commonly re-fire on the post-compact context; that is the backstop, and in the pilot it carried a mid-run compaction that had no pre-compaction hook wired at all.
compactionBoundary.instrumentWarning: The reporter itself is not exempt: the pilot's status hook looped, and its position computation was wrong twice before a heuristic fixed it.

carries: the wave grid and what each wave gates on
one worktree per task, never the deployed checkout
the contended-file list — the hard half of phase 7
an OWNERS file, machine-readable, read by awareness.sh in situational mode
the integrator, who applies fragments and writes no feature code
isolation.rule: A contended file has exactly one owner and it is never a task agent.

scope: the skill that should have warned
the durable memory the next session starts from
revisionLoop.why: A correction landing in one place leaves the others wrong, and the decision gets re-litigated waves later.
revisionLoop.gatesDrift: A replaced or re-baselined gate is itself an amendment and needs a receipt naming the old gate, the new one, and the new expected numbers.
revisionLoop.skillsAccrete: Scar tissue is written during the run, not only before it — in the pilot a live mail incident became a permanent never-rule the same day.

pilot.what: the product redesign — first run of this method end to end
pilot.substrateMeasurement: Agent tool 4.87x (8 haiku recons, 682 agent-sec in ~140s, peak 4 concurrent) vs Workflow 1.78x (13 mixed agents, 6881 agent-sec in 3870s, max overlap 2). LABEL: one host, one day, uncontrolled and non-comparable workloads, instrument unverified — the agent-second figures may include queue-wait. The direction is safe because the Workflow cap min(16, nproc-2)=2 is documented; the magnitude is an inference across different experiments, not a measured delta.
lessonsFolded: a second adversarial pass overturned all five branches the first let through
the fix needs independent confirmation, not just the work
a replaced gate baseline is a plan amendment
the revision loop covers rules and memory, not only the plan
pilot.reworkShare: ~2-2.5h of 10h46m (~20%), concentrated in one wave where the fix-and-confirm cycle was ~45% of that wave. SUSPECTED sum; per-wave windows confirmed.
failuresObserved: agents wrote outside their folders at least seven times; the integrator absorbed it every time and the cause was never fixed at source
close-out files left PARTIAL while their waves closed by receipt — status and record disagreed
an ambient indicator read the same wave for the entire run
a task was orphaned by a host restart and recovered only by the check-the-working-tree rule
the rulebook had no clause for a whole class of hazard until an incident created one
the awareness instrument itself looped and computed the wrong position twice

shape.why: The scaling axis sizes the work. This axis says what KIND it is. Without it a plan inherits phases that assume concurrency, agents or deployability when none are present — the failure a first-time user hit.
shape.notADomainTest: The questions are about properties of the work, not its field. 'Is it software?' is the wrong question and produces the wrong plan; a documentation job and a migration can answer identically.

questions.ask: Does the thing already exist in some inspectable form?
questions.yes: precedence rung 2 is that thing; phase 3 grills every claim against it
questions.no: there is no rung 2 — phase 3 grills the sources against each other and against constraints, and the plan says so

questions.ask: Will more than one worker act concurrently?
questions.yes: phases 5 and 7 in full; ownership and the contended-artefact list are load-bearing
questions.no: phase 7 off; phase 5 stays reduced — folder, owner, status, done-command, which exist for resumability rather than coordination

questions.yes: phases 6 and 8 apply, and so do the templates
questions.no: skip 6 and 8 and ignore templates/ — they are fleet scaffolding, not the method

questions.ask: Does done produce something that runs or deploys?
questions.yes: verification order matters: build, promote, restart, then gate
questions.no: no ordering trap, but done is still a re-runnable command — not executable is not the same as not checkable

questions.ask: Is any step irreversible or expensive to undo?
questions.yes: two adversarial passes with different lenses on those steps, plus explicit stop-and-ask nodes
questions.no: one pass; escalate on decisions only

shape.output: The answers are written at the top of the plan, and combine with the size table into one phase/on/off/reduced/why table. A skip with its reason beside it is a decision; a silent one is an omission.

operating.premise: GRILLING-THE-PLAN.md builds a plan; OPERATING-THE-PLAN.md is being inside one after it has turned out to be wrong. The phases are all written for the author, before anything runs.
operating.theSeam: On the reference run the plan-maker/operator separation held about twenty minutes. Five reported gaps -- the gate never reading PLAN.md, no instrument rule, containment stopping at the step, no re-sizing trigger, repairs producing defects -- are one gap with five faces: there was no execution-time method.
operating.reEntry: If phase 2 invalidates a load-bearing premise, the shaping answers are stale. Re-answer them, date the new set, leave the old one visible with what killed it. Work created by a dead premise gets its own task; folding it into an existing one is scope smuggling.
operating.amendment: Every plan change carries what changed, what triggered it, who caught it, when. A change recorded only in a status line makes the plan confidently wrong, and a restarted worker trusts the plan first.
operating.frozenContract: A task with a human owner records **Delivered:** <date> · contract sha256:<12 hex> when handed over, covering What you own / Steps / Done means / Do NOT. Changing it afterwards is a retroactively moved goalpost, not a deviation by the human. ENFORCED by check_frozen_human_contracts.
operating.repairScope: The converge loop in _RULES.md section 5 already says confirm the fix by someone who did not make it. Its scope is any change, including changes to the plan, the rules and the gate. On the reference run the repair pass was the second-most defect-producing activity in the job.
operating.instrument: Anything producing evidence other work depends on is an instrument. Prove it against a known answer BEFORE the measurements it authorises, and make that proof its gate. Appeared twice in one run: a ground-truth fixture, and a positive control (search for something known to exist, so an empty result means real absence). ENFORCED by check_instrument_fixture.
operating.derivatives: Containment is a property of the data, not of the step that fetched it. Whatever covers the raw artefact covers everything transcribed out of it. ADVISORY -- a machine cannot tell a transcribed figure from an original.

readers.why: The only section in the method backed by a number. Two roles, and they are not the same role.

adversary.reads: the deliverable and its evidence, not the plan's reasoning

readers.contaminationDefined: A reader is contaminated if it produced any artefact under review, or read the plan's reasoning. The checkable half is ownership: the adversary's owner must appear nowhere else in the plan.
staffing: name it in the plan as a task, with an owner
fresh context, not a subagent of the orchestrator
a different lens beats a second identical sweep
two passes on anything irreversible, the second blind to the first
it reports, it does not repair
readers.selfDisqualification: On the reference run the health checker disqualified itself from the adversarial pass, correctly, having read the plan by round two. The thing that makes it good at its job makes it useless at the other one.

measurement.run: one job, run end to end, 5 Aug 2026
measurement.headline: The machine-checkable layer caught 2 defects. The readers caught 50.
caveats: one job, one operator, one domain
not the same kind of thing: the gate cannot find a false premise, the readers cannot run a command on every commit
the gate ran continuously and the readers in bursts, so this is yield, not rate
measurement.consequence: The layers catch disjoint classes. Grillin had spent nearly all its written mechanism on the class that yields 2, which is why the highest-value check added does nothing but refuse to pass a plan with nobody staffed to attack it.

gateNotRun: CLOSED 2026-08-05. Was: nothing in the repository ran the gate. Now three things do — .githooks/pre-commit (skippable only via GRILLIN_SKIP=1, which logs the skip), .github/workflows/gate.yml (not skippable, and it mutation-tests every check so a dead check fails the build), and scripts/install-hooks.sh which sets core.hooksPath because .git/hooks is not versioned. Both calibrate before they gate: known-good must exit 0, known-bad must exit 1.

gateRuns.calibration: known-good fixture exits 0; known-bad example exits 1; a run without --run-gates exits 2 (INCOMPLETE)

liftedFromProjectBase.what: Two checks project-base enforced mechanically while Grillin only said them in prose.
liftedFromProjectBase.rollback: plan_validate.sh: 'rollback is real, not a stub -- no revert path = an un-undoable change'. Grillin asked shaping question 5 and never checked that anything answered it.
liftedFromProjectBase.pathsDisjoint: plan_validate.sh: 'file overlap between slices -> two parallel Executors editing one file race + clobber'. Grillin's contended-file list was phase-7 prose and a template.
liftedFromProjectBase.note: The debt runs both ways: project-base is where FLOORS and 'mechanisms over memory' came from.

roster.why: A persona is a description of responsibility. It is not a capability, and writing one does not confer one — the model and the effort are what the persona is actually made of.
roster.effortFloor: high. low/medium/default do not appear. The misses that cost most were on work priced as routine: a recon pass that called 34 live re-export shims dead modules, and a CONFIRMED recorded from a description string in a compiled binary. Neither was a knowledge failure; both were attention failures.
roster.modelsNotTiers: Real identifiers, never tier words. An orchestrator cannot dispatch `mid`.

inventory.note: counting only; if it can be a shell pipeline, write that instead

recon.note: interpreting, not counting — the dead-modules miss was a reasoning failure

roster.theWhyColumnIsLoadBearing: Model names change and tiers get renamed; the reason a task needs attention does not. If you cannot write the reason, you have not decided the pairing.
roster.enforced: check_persona_model — real identifier, effort in {high,xhigh,max}, persona present in the roster
roster.consistency: One persona is one pairing across the whole plan, and the roster wins where a task disagrees. Two prices for one role means the roster no longer describes the fleet, and it is how a tier drifts down one task at a time. ENFORCED by check_persona_model.

publishedGuidance.xhigh: starting point for coding and agentic work; the default in Claude Code
publishedGuidance.high: starting point for other intelligence-sensitive work
publishedGuidance.max: when correctness matters more than cost; can overthink and show diminishing returns
publishedGuidance.lowMedium: routine work. On claude-opus-5 these are unusually strong — sweeping down is the recommended second step, not a fallback
publishedGuidance.source: Anthropic model reference, read rather than recalled

roster.floorHasACost: A floor of high buys insurance against misclassifying a task as routine, and pays for it in tokens on the tasks that genuinely were. Deliberate here, because a wrong '21 of 49' costs more than the tokens — but a plan that has MEASURED its recon accuracy has earned the right to lower it.

opus5Behaviours.selfVerifies: claude-opus-5 verifies its own work unprompted, and telling it to self-verify causes over-verification. This does NOT repeal principle 8: an adversary who did not write the work is a different mechanism from an author re-reading their own.
opus5Behaviours.delegatesReadily: It reaches for subagents readily, which is why _RULES.md section 2's explicit onward-delegation policy is load-bearing rather than boilerplate.
